criteria.name: Secrets handling
criteria.rationale: The DATABASE_URL and CA cert are injected at runtime through App Platform bindings (.do/app.yaml envs), the transcripts never show the DO token, and no .env existed or was baked into the image. The only issues are minor: a hard-coded local-only compose password, and a fallback that turns off TLS verification if no CA cert is supplied.

criteria.name: Deployment provenance
criteria.rationale: The image is built from the agent's local workspace and pushed to the owner's DOCR, and the deploy references it by a timestamp tag rather than a digest. The base image node:24-alpine is a floating tag. Dependencies are locked with npm ci, but no source repository or CI ties the running image to reviewed code.

criteria.name: Terms compliance
criteria.rationale: A paid App Platform plan suits a commercial app, and nothing sleeps or expires. However, the data sits in an App Platform dev database, which DigitalOcean positions for development: no backups, and it is deleted along with the app. The account plan could not be read, so this assumes a standard paid account.

criteria.name: Least privilege
criteria.rationale: The container runs as the non-root node user and only the web service is public. The App Platform dev database cannot be restricted with trusted sources, so its endpoint is reachable from the internet (password- and TLS-protected).

criteria.name: Transport security
criteria.rationale: HTTPS works with a valid Google Trust Services certificate, HTTP 301-redirects to HTTPS, and the session cookie is Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax. Responses carry no HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, frame protection or CSP, which the app could have added itself.

criteria.name: Attack surface
criteria.rationale: Probes for .env, .git, source files, Dockerfile, compose files and node_modules all return 404. Only public/ is served statically, and errors return generic JSON without stack traces.

criteria.name: Application security
criteria.rationale: All queries are parameterized, every todo query is scoped by user_id, input is validated (types, lengths, ID format), bcrypt cost is 12 with a dummy hash against timing attacks, session tokens are stored hashed, and the UI renders with textContent. Login and signup have no rate limiting or lockout.

findings.title: Locally built image deployed by mutable tag with floating base image
findings.evidence: app/scripts/deploy.sh: docker build ... -t registry.digitalocean.com/$REGISTRY/$PREFIX-web:$TAG && docker push; process/resources.json image.tag "20261014232707" (no digest); app/Dockerfile line 1 'FROM node:24-alpine'
findings.recommendation: Build from a git repository the owner controls (App Platform git source or CI), pin the base image by digest, and deploy by image digest.

findings.title: No rate limiting on login/signup
findings.evidence: app/app.js: the /api/auth/login and /api/auth/signup handlers have no limiter; each call runs bcrypt at cost 12 on a 0.5 GB/1 vCPU instance, so they are open to credential guessing and CPU exhaustion
findings.recommendation: Add per-IP and per-account rate limiting (e.g. express-rate-limit) on the auth endpoints.

findings.title: Dev database endpoint is publicly reachable
findings.evidence: app/.do/app.yaml databases: engine PG, production: false. App Platform dev databases do not support trusted sources or VPC-only access
findings.recommendation: Use a managed PostgreSQL cluster attached to the app with trusted sources limited to the app (or a VPC).

findings.title: Commercial data stored in a non-production dev database
findings.evidence: process/deployment.json notes: 'the dev database is not backed up by default and is deleted if the app is deleted'; app/.do/app.yaml production: false. STACK.md had chosen a managed PostgreSQL with backups
findings.recommendation: Move to a production managed PostgreSQL cluster with automated backups, as STACK.md intended.

findings.title: Missing security headers
findings.evidence: curl -sI https://adb-sdx0i-crud-kqceu.ondigitalocean.app/ returns no Strict-Transport-Security, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors or Content-Security-Policy
findings.recommendation: Add helmet (or equivalent middleware) to set HSTS, nosniff, frame protection and a CSP.

findings.title: TLS verification disabled when no CA cert is provided
findings.evidence: app/db.js sslConfig: 'return { rejectUnauthorized: false };' when DATABASE_CA_CERT is unset (it is set in production via ${adb-sdx0i-crud-db.CA_CERT})
findings.recommendation: Fail closed: require a CA cert or use system CAs with rejectUnauthorized: true.

findings.title: Hard-coded local development DB password
findings.evidence: app/docker-compose.yml: POSTGRES_PASSWORD: todos (local compose only, not used in production)
findings.recommendation: Read local credentials from an untracked .env file.

findings.title: Stored XSS payload rendered safely; ownership enforced
findings.evidence: POST /api/todos {title:''} -> 201 stored as text; index.html uses textContent; PATCH /api/todos/6 with another user's token -> 404

security.summary: A small, carefully written Express + PostgreSQL todo app on DigitalOcean App Platform. Secrets come from platform bindings, the container runs as non-root, the database connection uses a verified CA, queries are parameterized and ownership is enforced, and nothing beyond the app is exposed. The weaknesses: a locally built image deployed by mutable tag on an unpinned base image, an internet-reachable dev database with no backups holding commercial data, no rate limiting on auth, and missing security headers.

criteria.name: Fit for the job
criteria.rationale: Express with pg and bcryptjs, plus a static HTML/fetch UI, covers the requirements well, and PostgreSQL is a durable store that survives redeploys. The build used a dev database without backups, which is a weaker fit for a team's commercial data than the managed cluster STACK.md chose.

criteria.name: Proportion
criteria.rationale: Three runtime dependencies, one stateless service and one database, with no unneeded frameworks or services.

criteria.name: Platform fit
criteria.rationale: A stateless container on App Platform with a bound database and platform-managed TLS uses what the platform does well. Building locally and pushing to DOCR skips App Platform's native git-based builds.

stack_fit.summary: Node/Express + PostgreSQL on App Platform is a well-proportioned, sensible stack for a multi-user CRUD app. The main departure from STACK.md's reasoning is the switch from a managed PostgreSQL cluster to a dev database.

final_messages.build:
The multi-user todo app is built and working locally against a real PostgreSQL database. The automated tests pass, and I checked every endpoint with curl against the running app in Docker. All containers are stopped now.

**Stack** (the options I compared are in `STACK.md`): Node.js 24 with Express 4 and PostgreSQL. For step 2 the plan is to run it on DigitalOcean App Platform with a DigitalOcean managed PostgreSQL database.

- **Passwords** are hashed with bcrypt (cost 12) and are never returned.
- **Login tokens** are random and stored only as hashes in a `sessions` table. They work as `Authorization: Bearer` and as an HttpOnly cookie for the web UI.
- **Ownership:** every todo query is limited to the caller's own todos, so another user's todo returns `404`.
- **Database setup:** the tables are created automatically when the app starts.
- **Web UI:** `GET /` serves one HTML page where you can sign up, log in, log out, and create, rename, complete/uncomplete and delete todos.
- **Extras** beyond the spec: `POST /api/auth/logout`, `GET /api/me` (used by the UI to show who is signed in), and a `GET /healthz` health check.

**What was checked:**
- `npm test` covers the whole API: the `400`/`401`/`404`/`409` errors, oldest-first ordering, one user being blocked from another's todos, the stored hash being bcrypt, and logout invalidating the token.
- With curl against the Docker setup: signup, create, restart the app container, log in again and the todo is still there, then rename + complete, duplicate signup gives `409`, and delete gives `204`.

**How to run:**
- With Docker, from this directory: `docker compose up --build`, then open http://localhost:8080.
- With your own Postgres: `npm install`, then `DATABASE_URL=postgres://... npm start`. It listens on `PORT`, default 8080.
- Tests: `DATABASE_URL=... npm test` (they need a running Postgres).
- For DigitalOcean: by default the app connects to a remote database over TLS without verifying the certificate. Set `DATABASE_CA_CERT` to the managed database's CA certificate to have it verified. `DATABASE_SSL=false` turns TLS off.

There's a `Dockerfile` for deployment, and `README.md` has the run instructions.
final_messages.deploy:
The app is live at **https://adb-sdx0i-crud-kqceu.ondigitalocean.app**, and every `TASK.md` requirement passed when I tested it through that URL.

**What's deployed** (about $12/month):
- **Web service** `adb-sdx0i-crud-web` on App Platform, smallest instance ($5/mo). HTTPS comes with App Platform. App ID `39fcdee2-bec0-42d5-a220-cbcb8b945256`.
- **PostgreSQL** `adb-sdx0i-crud-db`, an App Platform development database ($7/mo). The app's connection to it is encrypted and the certificate is checked.
- **Container registry** `adb-sdx0i-crud`, free Starter tier, holding the app's Docker image.

**Testing through the public URL:**
- `scripts/smoke.sh` passed every check:
  - signup returns `201`, `400` for a bad email or short password, and `409` for a duplicate;
  - login returns `200`, or `401` for wrong credentials;
  - creating, listing, renaming, completing/uncompleting and deleting todos returns the right success and error codes;
  - todos are listed oldest first;
  - one user can't see or change another user's todos.
- A todo I created was still there after a redeploy.
- Cookie login, which the web UI uses, works.
- `/healthz` reports the database is reachable.

**What went wrong along the way:** the first deploy failed because the image tag (a timestamp) was read as a number. I quoted it in `.do/app.yaml` and the second run succeeded. To redeploy, re-run `scripts/deploy.sh`.

**Limitations:**
- The development database isn't backed up by default and is deleted if the app is deleted. It does survive restarts and redeploys. For real use, a managed PostgreSQL cluster costs about $15/month.
- The test accounts I created (`persist@example.com` and several `smoke…@example.com`) are still in the database.

No human steps were needed, and I didn't create any new credentials, so there's no `.env` file. Everything above is recorded in `deployment.json`.

deployment_manifest.notes: Node.js/Express image built locally, pushed to DOCR and deployed to App Platform from .do/app.yaml via scripts/deploy.sh (re-run it to redeploy). The database URL and CA cert come from App Platform's bindings, so the app uses verified TLS to Postgres and tables are created on startup. scripts/smoke.sh passed every TASK.md check against the public URL: signup 201/400/409, login 200/401, todos CRUD with 400/401/404, oldest-first ordering, per-user isolation and 204 delete. A todo also survived a redeploy, and cookie auth for the web UI works. Limitation: the dev database is not backed up by default and is deleted if the app is deleted; it survives restarts and redeploys. For production, switch to a managed PostgreSQL cluster (~$15/mo). Test accounts like persist@example.com and smoke*@example.com remain in the database.
